case.case_title: Kumara vs. Silva, Sub-Inspector of Police, Welipenna and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (2006) 2 Sri L R. 236

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was arrested in accordance with the procedure established by law and informed of the reason for arrest as required by Article 13(1).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was arbitrarily arrested on 03.02.2004 at about 8.30 a.m. without proper legal procedure and was assaulted.
case_context.respondent_argument: The 1st respondent argued the petitioner was arrested on 05.02.2004 at about 6.45 p.m. based on credible information and reasonable suspicion related to armed robbery and possession of weapons, in accordance with law.
key_facts: Petitioner was taken to police station on 03.02.2004 but arrest was claimed to have occurred on 05.02.2004 according to respondent.
Arrest was based on complaint of armed robbery and information from informants.
Petitioner was produced before Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest as per respondent.
Petitioner alleged assault and torture after arrest.
Medical evidence showed injuries but did not contradict lawful arrest.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(1) requires arrests to be made according to procedure established by law and not arbitrarily. Arrests without warrant are permitted if reasonable suspicion or credible information exists. The court emphasized that Article 13(1) does not prohibit arrests but prohibits arbitrary arrests.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court accepted the 1st respondent’s version supported by investigation notes and affidavits that the petitioner was arrested on 05.02.2004 based on credible information and reasonable suspicion. The petitioner was informed and produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours. Therefore, the arrest complied with Article 13(1).
principles_established: Arrest must follow procedure established by law and not be arbitrary.
Reasonable suspicion or credible information justifies arrest without warrant.
Arresting officers must inform the arrested person of the reason for arrest.
precedents_cited: Eshugbabai vs. Government of Nigeria 1931 AC 238

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s arrest was not in violation of Article 13(1) of the Constitution.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) was central to determining whether the petitioner’s arrest was lawful and non-arbitrary, which was a key issue in the case.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The 1st respondent arrested the petitioner on 05.02.2004 based on credible information and reasonable suspicion, supported by investigation notes and affidavits; the petitioner was produced before the Magistrate within 24 hours.
